REPORT
Date July 10, 1931
Subject (in full) Don Chisholm.
Made by D. S. Moore. Forwarded by (签名)
Following the publication of the Shanghai Evening Post
and Mercury on 27-4-31 bearing the attached cutting, a protest
was sent to the Editor of the paper by Mr. Carroll Lunt of the
"China Digest" and representative in Shanghai and adjoining
territory of the International News Service. According further
enquiries were instituted by the newspaper in an effort to
substantiate the truth or otherwise of Chisholm's statement that
he had been appointed Shanghai representative of the Hearst
newspaper group.
The reply to their enquiring cablegram reads as follows:-
"30-4-31 Chisholm has no connection whatever with Internews".
Montee, Director of Foreign Service. Upon receipt of this, Chisholm
was called to the office of the newspaper to explain his previous
claims and the same evening (30-4-31) the paper published a letter
from Chisholm to the Editor apologising for any inconvenience
caused to Mr. Carroll Lunt: and also a letter from Mr. Lunt
stating that he was the sole representative in Shanghai of the
I.N. Service.
It has been previously reported that Chisholm had been
admitted as a member of the local American Chamber of Commerce.
This is a misstatement of fact, for at that time he was only an
honorary member and when his name was submitted for election to
full membership, it was rejected.
At the present time he is employed by H.E.Booker on
publicity work for the Luna Park Amusement Resort.
D. S. Moore
Officer i/c Special Branch.
(批：long gone away 4/7)
(批：Regd 15/7 D.C. (Crime) Information J.P. Liverno 16.8.31)

日期 1931年7月10日
主题（全称）唐·奇斯霍尔姆 (Don Chisholm)。
制作人 D. S. Moore。转发人 (签名)
继4月27日《上海晚邮报及信使报》(Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury) 刊登所附剪报后，《中国文摘》(China Digest) 的卡罗尔·伦特 (Carroll Lunt) 先生暨国际新闻社 (International News Service) 驻上海及周边地区代表向该报编辑提出抗议。据此，该报展开进一步调查，以证实或证伪奇斯霍尔姆关于其已被任命为赫斯特 (Hearst) 报业集团上海代表的说法。
对其查询电报的回复如下：-
“31年4月30日 奇斯霍尔姆与国际新闻社 (Internews) 毫无关联”。
外事部主任蒙蒂 (Montee)。收到此回复后，奇斯霍尔姆被召至报社办公室，就其先前的声称作出解释；同日晚上（31年4月30日），该报刊登了奇斯霍尔姆致编辑的一封信，就给卡罗尔·伦特先生造成的任何不便表示歉意；同时也刊登了伦特先生的一封信，声明他是国际新闻社在上海的唯一代表。
此前曾有报告称，奇斯霍尔姆已被接纳为当地美国商会的会员。
这是对事实的错误陈述，因为当时他仅为荣誉会员，且当其名字被提交选举为正式会员时，遭到了拒绝。
目前，他受雇于 H.E. Booker，负责月园游乐场 (Luna Park Amusement Resort) 的宣传工作。
D. S. Moore
特别课主管警官。

Date 25 / 2 / 36

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, February 27, 1936

To Chaliapin
To the Editor:
Apparently the concerts of Mr.
Chaliapin are both financially and
socially a tremendous success, in
all probability this gentleman will
leave our fair city some $1500
wealthier than when he arrived.
This is not to be begrudged, for
the master, though not so young
as he was, still gives a gorgeous
performance.
But what we have in mind is this.
Chaliapin is a Russian and here in
Shanghai there are thousands of
his fellow countrymen in need
of help and charity. America has
made great efforts to bring
assistance to these refugees and
other nationalities in similar plight.
Why should not a small part of
the fortune made by this famous
singer be devoted to helping his
own people? It is true that previous
visits from singers have met with
similar from singing for charity!
After all Chaliapin's splendid
voice is a gift to him from his
maker. Ought he not for once
share with the less fortunate of his
countrymen who have been less
fortunate than himself?

INTERNATIONAL SETTLEMENT
MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
Shanghai, Feb. 26, 1936.

$2, Please pass to
Reg. to file.
JAS.

《上海晚邮报及信使报》，1936年2月27日，星期四

致夏里亚平
致编辑：
显然，夏里亚平 (Chaliapin) 先生的音乐会在财务上和社交上都取得了巨大的成功，这位先生离开我们这座美丽的城市时，很可能比到来时多赚了1500美元。
这并不令人嫉妒，因为这位大师虽然不再像以前那样年轻，但依然奉献了精彩的演出。
但我们心里想的是这一点。
夏里亚平是俄罗斯人，而在上海，有成千上万他的同胞需要帮助和慈善。美国已做出巨大努力，为这些难民以及其他处于类似困境国籍的人提供援助。
为什么这位著名歌手赚取的财富中，不拿出一小部分来帮助他自己的人民呢？诚然，此前歌手的来访也遇到过类似情况，即通过演唱进行慈善募捐！
毕竟，夏里亚平美妙的嗓音是造物主赐予他的礼物。他难道不应该一次与他那些比他不幸的、境遇较差的同胞分享吗？

公共租界
工部局
上海，1936年2月26日。

$2，请转交
登记处归档。
JAS.
1936年2月26日

Shanghai
Land & Lat.
Shanghai, Monday,

Takes Over New Post

MR. DON CHISHOLM

Don Chisholm New
Hearst Man Here

I. N. S. Correspondent
Has Circled Globe
Several Times

Shanghai's latest addition to the ranks of foreign correspondents is Mr. Don Chisholm, of Charleston, South Carolina. Mr. Chisholm is staff correspondent and special writer for the International News Service, the great news gathering and distributing agency owned by Mr. William Randolph Hearst, American newspaper magnate. In addition, Mr. Chisholm, who is widely travelled, having made several trips around the world, is regarded as an authority on political economy, especially in certain European, South and Central American countries.

In 1934 Mr. Chisholm, then a rising young newspaperman, attracted the attention of the Hearst organization, the result being an offer which he accepted. He has been more or less actively connected with the organization since and has "covered" some of the outstanding news stories, political and otherwise, of America and other countries during the past few years.

Correspondent For Papers
In addition to representing International News Service in European cities, where he was stationed for some time, Mr. Chisholm has served as representative for New York and Washington dailies, contributing timely articles on political economy, silver, etc. He returned to the United States from Europe in 1936 and became associated with the News and Journal of Dallas, Texas.

Later he was sent to South America, visiting Buenos Aires, Rio de Janeiro and other cities and making also a trip up the Amazon River for a special story on the rubber holdings of Henry Ford and the Goodyear interests.

Came Here In 1935
In the same year he came to China and again visited here in 1937. In all, he has visited China eight times and has a number of friends in this country.

During his last few months in Los Angeles, prior to coming here, Mr. Chisholm was identified with the Los Angeles Chamber of Commerce, in the foreign trade department, interested in the creating and development of Oriental trade. He was instrumental in putting through a resolution whereby the chamber called upon California newspapers to cease publishing news concerning China unless of a constructive nature.

Since his arrival here Mr. Chisholm has taken over the interests of the I. N. S. He represents also the North American Newspaper Alliance, the Baltimore Sun and San Francisco Chronicle.

上海，星期一，

接任新职

唐·奇斯霍尔姆先生

唐·奇斯霍尔姆
赫斯特报业新任驻沪人员

国际新闻社记者
曾数次环球旅行

上海外国记者队伍中的最新成员是来自南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿的唐·奇斯霍尔姆先生。奇斯霍尔姆先生是美国报业巨头威廉·伦道夫·赫斯特 (William Randolph Hearst) 先生拥有的大型新闻采集与分发机构——国际新闻社 (International News Service) 的专职记者和特约撰稿人。此外，奇斯霍尔姆先生游历广泛，曾数次环球旅行，被视为政治经济学方面的权威，特别是在某些欧洲、南美和中美洲国家。

1934年，当时作为一名崭露头角的年轻报人，奇斯霍尔姆先生引起了赫斯特机构的注意，结果是他接受了一份聘书。自那时起，他便与该机构保持着或多或少的活跃联系，并在过去几年中“报道”了美国及其他国家的一些突出新闻故事，包括政治和其他方面。

多家报纸的通讯员
除了在曾驻扎一段时间的欧洲城市代表国际新闻社外，奇斯霍尔姆先生还曾担任纽约和华盛顿日报的代表，撰写有关政治经济学、白银等的时事文章。他于1936年从欧洲返回美国，并与德克萨斯州达拉斯的《新闻报》(News) 和《期刊报》(Journal) 建立了合作关系。

后来他被派往南美洲，访问了布宜诺斯艾利斯、里约热内卢和其他城市，并沿亚马逊河进行了一次旅行，为关于亨利·福特 (Henry Ford) 和固特异 (Goodyear) 利益集团的橡胶持有量的专题报道搜集素材。

1935年来华
同年他来到中国，并于1937年再次访问此地。总的来说，他曾八次访问中国，并在这个国家拥有许多朋友。

在来此之前的最后几个月里，奇斯霍尔姆先生在洛杉矶期间，任职于洛杉矶商会对外贸易部，致力于东方贸易的创建和发展。他促成了一项决议，促使商会呼吁加州报纸停止发布有关中国的新闻，除非是具有建设性的内容。

自抵达此地以来，奇斯霍尔姆先生已接管国际新闻社的业务。他还代表北美报业联盟 (North American Newspaper Alliance)、《巴尔的摩太阳报》(Baltimore Sun) 和《旧金山纪事报》(San Francisco Chronicle)。

Subject (in full) Don Chisolm.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Duncan.

Sir,

Enquiries show that Don Chisolm, American citizen, first arrived in Shanghai in September 1930. He was formerly employed as a stoker on board a Dollar Steamship Line boat. Soon after his arrival here, he appeared in the Cathay Hotel and attempted to obtain refreshments on credit on the strength that he was an employee of the Robert Dollar Coy. The Management of the Cathay rang up the Dollar Coy, and it was then learned that Chisolm had been a stoker on one of their boats but was no longer in their employ. Nevertheless he managed to obtain credit later on, and was finally warned by the Manager not to frequent the Hotel. It appears that he soon afterwards left for the U.S.A. and returned here on April 24, 1931.

On May 15th in company with a Miss Branch, daughter of Dr. Branch, No. 8 Route Adiena, French Concession, he went to the Cathay and had tiffin for which he signed a chit. The Manager, Mr. Campbell, called him from the table and told him that he could not be allowed to sign chits, and that he would have to pay cash for the tiffins. Chisolm said that he would do so and left Mr. Campbell but instead of returning to the table he walked out of the hotel leaving Miss Branch to pay for the tiffins.

Chisolm was recently admitted a member of the American Chamber of Commerce. He has also made arrangements with the Chinese-American Publishing Coy, No. 78 Nanking Road for a regular supply of American magazines.

5月15日，他与法租界亚迪纳路 (Route Adiena) 8号布兰奇博士 (Dr. Branch) 的女儿布兰奇小姐 (Miss Branch) 一同前往华懋饭店用午餐，并签单记账。经理坎贝尔 (Campbell) 先生将他从餐桌旁叫出，告诉他不允许签单，午餐必须付现金。奇索尔姆表示他会照办，并离开了坎贝尔先生，但他没有回到餐桌，而是走出了酒店，留下布兰奇小姐支付午餐费用。

Re attached reports, I visited Don Chisolm
at 8.30 a.m. 28.4.31 at his Room 701 Foreign Y.M.C.A.
He informed me that he obtained the 'fountain pen'
gun and ammunition in Los. Angeles from an agent
of the firm who make "Federal" gas. So far as
he knows there are no other such weapons in the
Far East.

The ammunition used, would fit an ordinary
.38 Cal. revolver, but if fired in such, would not
be so effective as with the 'fountain pen' gun which
has a choke bore.

Chisolm gave me a small bottle of the gas
crystals, with which the cartridges are loaded.
These crystals are not effective until ignited.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No.
REPORT
Yangtzepoo Station,
Date April 29 1931
Subject (in full) Further re Tear Gas (Fountain Pen) Pistol
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Wardrop

Sir,
On 27-4-31, enquiries were made at the French Special Branch, Avenue Joffre, and it was ascertained that the injuries which Bondreau received were caused by Chisolm at the Candidrom, French Concession, about 2 a.m. 26-4-31 and that the American Consular Authorities were aware of the occurrence.
Enquiries were made at the American Consulate and it was learned from Mr. Van Buskirk, that one "Don Chisholm", Correspondent for the International News Service, residing at the Foreign Y.M.C.A. Bubblingwell Road, had rung him up from the General Hospital, about 4 a.m. 26-4-31 and reported the incident. Mr. Van Buskirk attended at the Hospital, where he questioned the parties and asked the injured man if he wish to prefer a charge against Chisholm. This he declined to do.
Mr. Van Buskirk took charge of the (Fountain Pen) Pistol, and then allowed Chisholm to go. Dr. Sellett, American District Attorney, was also interviewed, and acquainted with the information against the accused, and he ordered Chisholm to be summoned to his office for enquiries.
On 29-4-31, undersigned again interviewed Dr. Sellett, and was informed that Chisholm had attended the District Attorney's Office on 28-4-31, when it was ascertained that he "Chisholm" had obtained the Fountain Pen Pistol in Los Angeles from a representative of a Pittsburg firm who were stated to have supplied tear gas materials to the Shanghai Municipal Police.
Dr. Sellett was convinced that "Chisholm" had no more of the Tear Gas (Fountain Pen) Pistols, and that he had no idea of trading in such articles.

主题（全称）再论催泪瓦斯（钢笔）手枪
制作及转发人 D.S.I. Wardrop

先生，
31年4月27日，向霞飞路 (Avenue Joffre) 的法国特别课进行了查询，获悉邦德罗 (Bondreau) 所受伤害是由奇索尔姆于31年4月26日凌晨2点左右在法租界康梯大花园 (Candidrom) 造成的，且美国领事当局已知晓此事。
向美国领事馆进行了查询，从范·布斯柯克 (Van Buskirk) 先生处获悉，一名名为“唐·奇什霍尔姆” (Don Chisholm)、国际新闻社记者、居住在静安寺路 (Bubblingwell Road) 青年会国际宾馆的人，曾于31年4月26日凌晨4点左右从广慈医院 (General Hospital) 给他打电话报告了这一事件。范·布斯柯克先生前往医院，在那里询问了各方当事人，并询问受伤者是否希望对奇索尔姆提出指控。受伤者拒绝这样做。
范·布斯柯克先生没收了（钢笔）手枪，然后允许奇索尔姆离开。美国地方检察官塞莱特 (Sellett) 博士也接受了问询，并获知了对被告的不利信息，他命令传唤奇索尔姆到其办公室接受调查。
31年4月29日，具名者再次会见了塞莱特博士，并获悉奇索尔姆已于31年4月28日到地方检察官办公室报到，当时查明“奇索尔姆”是从匹兹堡一家公司的代表那里获得这支钢笔手枪的，据说该公司曾向上海公共租界工部局警务处供应催泪瓦斯材料。

塞莱特博士确信“奇索尔姆”不再拥有更多的催泪瓦斯（钢笔）手枪，并且他无意从事此类物品的交易。

Subject (in full) Further re Tear Gas (Fountain Pen) Pistol
Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Hardrup

Sir,
On 27-4-31, enquiries were made at the French Special Branch, Avenue Joffre, and it was ascertained that the injuries which Bondreau received were caused by Chisholm at the Candidrome French Concession, about 1 a.m. 26-4-31 and that the American Consular Authorities were aware of the occurrence.
Inquiries were made at the American Consulate and it was learned from Mr. Van Buskirk, that one "Don Chisholm", Correspondent for the International News Service, residing at the Foreign Y.M.C.A. Bubblingwell Road, had rung him up from the General Hospital, about 4 a.m. 26-4-31 and reported the incident. Mr. Van Buskirk attended at the Hospital, where he questioned the parties and asked the injured man if he wish to prefer a charge against Chisholm. This he declined to do.
Mr. Van Buskirk took charge of the (Fountain Pen) Pistol, and then allowed Chisholm to go. Dr. Sellett, American District Attorney, was also interviewed, and acquainted with the information against the accused, and he ordered Chisholm to be summoned to his office for enquiries.
On 29-4-31, undersigned again interviewed Dr. Sellett, and was informed that Chisholm had attended the District Attorney's Office on 28-4-31, when it was ascertained that he "Chisholm" had obtained the Fountain Pen Pistol in Los Angeles from a representative of a Pittsburg firm who were stated to have supplied tear gas materials to the Shanghai Municipal Police.
Dr. Sellett was convinced that "Chisholm" had no more of the Tear Gas (Fountain Pen) Pistols, and that he had no idea of trading in such articles.

线人进一步称，他无意中听到“金阳”号船长告知他人，一名名为奇索姆的乘客在1931年4月25日（星期六）晚于上海某处饮酒时，将其中一支钢笔对着其面部发射，致使一名船员受伤，伤者目前住院，并将因此误船。
鉴于此，蒂尔顿（Tilton）副巡官前往广慈医院（General Hospital）进行调查，以核实上述报告的真实性，并查明了以下情况：-

THE NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, APRIL 28, 1931
857

FIGHT AMONG FRIENDS
Gas Bomb Used in Fray
in Cabaret
VICTIM REFUSES TO
PRESS CHARGE

A brawl occurred early on Sunday morning in the "largest ballroom in Shanghai" between two civilians, during the course of which the first gas bomb in Shanghai was utilized in a purely civilian affair. The victim was partially blinded for a number of hours and the aggressor, shocked with what he had done, took his opponent off to the General Hospital, where his injuries were attended to. He left Shanghai on his ship early yesterday morning.

Although on one occasion, the police called in British troops with bombs to overcome an armed bandit in the famous "Sydney Street" affair in Wayside two years ago, at no other time have either foreigners or Chinese resorted to gas to settle their differences. The weapon employed was a fountain pen mustard gas bomb.

The principals in Sunday's affair were two American citizens—the victim a quartermaster on the States Steamship Line str. Golden Sun and the other a passenger on the same vessel who disembarked from the vessel and took up quarters in the Foreign Y.M.C.A. The complainant before leaving port yesterday morning, said, in response to official queries, "I do not wish to take any action against him. He was a little drunk when he did it." Other than slight soreness and weakness to his eyes, the quartermaster left port yesterday uninjured.

Seeing Shanghai

According to the story of the complainant, the two met and decided to see Shanghai during Saturday night. They had a few drinks and later went to the Casanova cabaret, where peace and harmony reigned between the parties.

Moving on to another cabaret, they sat round for some time, having several drinks. In the course of a subsequent conversation, words passed between the quartermaster and his friend, who is now residing in Shanghai. The discussion became heated, words leading to invectives and the complainant challenged the other to a fight. They left the ballroom. On the way out it appears that they squared off, but others standing by intervened between them.

During the skirmish and their attempts to release themselves, the passengers of the Golden Sun managed partially to free himself and, reaching in his pocket, pulled out the "bombing machine". Pressing the button trigger, he released the charge, which at a distance of a few feet, was squirted into the other's face.

Taken to Hospital

With the victim screaming with pain from the mustard gas in his nostrils and eyes, the crowd came to his assistance. The aggressor suddenly came to his senses and after some minutes, a motor car having been called, went with his "friend" to the General Hospital. Attendants applied compresses, at once to the affected eyes and the quartermaster was put to bed.

This having been done the other telephoned to Settlement police and informed them, "I have shot a man," giving his address. Detectives—Det.-Sgt. Barton from Bubbling Well station, and others from Sinza attended—and on learning where the trouble had occurred, turned the case over to the French Police.

Their investigations in the meanwhile proved that the weapon was of American make, patented in 1925. Inasmuch as the complainant would not prefer a charge, the aggressor was not detained.

Although rumours were current yesterday that the quartermaster would lose the sight of one eye, they are stated as being untrue. He was discharged from the General Hospital at 5 p.m. on Sunday, and rejoined his ship which left port at daybreak yesterday. Other than temporary weakness, which should be eliminated within a few days at sea, he will, it is stated, suffer no inconvenience.

Sale Formerly Suppressed

In the past a number of various kinds of gas pistols have been offered for sale here, but on the police having received information of their public disposal, short shrift was given to the vendors. The weapon used on Sunday morning, however, differed from those on sale formerly. Whereas those were of continental make, of cast iron and quite heavy, this one is of American origin, patented in 1925.

It is made of aluminium, very light—not over five ounces in weight—and can be attached to a waist coat pocket without inconvenience. The "pistol" is "safe" for the holder, inasmuch as after it is cocked by pulling the butt back, the clip fits over the trigger button as a safety catch.

The barrel is shaped much like a rifle cartridge, about the size of a 30-30, with the orifice slightly smaller than a .38 calibre pistol. The ordinary gas pistol is loaded with a specially prepared cartridge, which is exploded when the firing pin strikes a cap. This weapon, it has been stated, can be used, however, when loaded with bulk "powder."

It is understood that the authorities will take steps to prevent further importation of the instruments into Shanghai, although this particular "pistol" is alleged to have been imported on the person of the passenger.

（手写批注：The publication of this account described in the above issue of the North China Daily News by Universal News Service, and others, will probably develop a new source of trouble for the Police.）

（签名：D.B. (Crime) / Pained boyon. / W.J. Gweno / 0.4c Sp. Br. 28/4/31）

《字林西报》，1931年4月28日，星期二
857

朋友间的斗殴
舞厅冲突中使用瓦斯弹
受害者拒绝起诉

周日清晨，在“上海最大的舞厅”里，两名平民之间发生了一场斗殴，期间上海首次在一桩纯粹的民事纠纷中使用了瓦斯弹。受害者双眼暂时失明数小时，肇事者对自己所为感到震惊，将对手送往总医院接受治疗。他于昨天清晨乘船离开上海。

尽管两年前在著名的“悉尼街”事件中，警方曾调用携带炸弹的英军士兵以制服一名武装匪徒，但在此之前，无论是外国人还是中国人，都未曾诉诸瓦斯来解决争端。所使用的武器是一支钢笔式芥子气弹。

周日事件的主要当事人是两名美国公民——受害者是美国轮船公司“金阳”号（str. Golden Sun）上的军需官，另一人是同一艘船上的乘客，该乘客已下船并在青年会（Foreign Y.M.C.A.）住宿。投诉人在昨天清晨离港前，回应官方询问时表示：“我不希望对他采取任何行动。他当时有点喝醉了。”除了眼睛轻微酸痛和无力外，该军需官昨天离港时并未受伤。

游览上海

根据投诉人的叙述，两人相遇并决定在周六晚上游览上海。他们喝了几杯酒，随后去了卡萨诺瓦（Casanova）舞厅，当时双方气氛平和融洽。

随后他们转到另一家舞厅，坐了一段时间，又喝了几杯酒。在随后的谈话中，军需官与他那位现居上海的朋友发生了口角。讨论变得激烈，言语升级为辱骂，投诉人向对方提出决斗挑战。他们离开了舞厅。在出去的路上，他们似乎摆开了架势准备打斗，但旁观者介入其间进行了劝阻。

在混战及试图脱身的过程中，“金阳”号的乘客设法部分挣脱出来，伸手进口袋，掏出了那件“轰炸机器”。按下按钮扳机，他释放了装药，在几英尺的距离外，将其喷射到对方面部。

送医治疗

受害者因鼻孔和眼睛吸入芥子气而痛苦尖叫，人群上前协助。肇事者突然清醒过来，几分钟后，叫来一辆汽车，与他的“朋友”一同前往总医院。医护人员立即对受影响的眼睛敷上压缩绷带，将军需官安置在床上。

做完这些后，另一方打电话给租界警方，告知他们：“我开枪打了一个人”，并提供了自己的地址。侦探——来自静安寺警署的巴顿（Barton）警长及其他来自新闸警署的人员——到场，在得知事发地点后，将案件移交给法国警方。

与此同时，他们的调查证实，该武器为美国制造，于1925年获得专利。由于投诉人不愿提出指控，肇事者未被拘留。

尽管昨天有谣言称该军需官将失去一只眼睛的视力，但据称这些谣言不实。他于周日下午5点从总医院出院，并回到船上，该船于昨天黎明时分离港。据称，除了暂时的虚弱（预计在海上的几天内即可消除）外，他不会受到任何不便。

此前销售曾被取缔

过去，这里曾出售过多种不同类型的气体手枪，但当警方获悉其公开销售的情报后，商贩们受到了严厉处置。然而，周日早上使用的武器与以前出售的不同。以前的大陆制造品由铸铁制成，相当沉重，而这一支源自美国，于1925年获得专利。

它由铝制成，非常轻——重量不超过五盎司——可以方便地附在马甲口袋上。这支“手枪”对持有者是“安全”的，因为当向后拉动枪柄上膛后，夹子会盖住触发按钮作为保险栓。

枪管形状很像步枪子弹，大小约为.30-30口径，孔径略小于.38口径手枪。普通的气体手枪装载特制子弹，当击针撞击底火时子弹爆炸。然而，据说这种武器在装载散装“粉末”时也可以使用。

据悉，当局将采取措施防止此类器械进一步进口到上海，尽管据称这支特定的“手枪”是由该乘客随身携带入境的。

（手写批注：《字林西报》上述期刊中由环球新闻社（Universal News Service）及其他机构发布的这篇报道，可能会给警方带来新的麻烦源头。）

（签名：D.B. (刑事科) / Pained boyon. / W.J. Gweno / 0.4c 特别分部 1931年4月28日）
